title: Power Platform governance: multi-grader comparison for agent evaluations
notes: claim 27: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: the briefing says evaluation automation is undocumented, but Microsoft publishes a Power Platform REST API for running evaluations and retrieving results. It also transfers existing Copilot Studio permissions, controls and consumption assumptions to a feature whose product surface is still unconfirmed, and presents an incomplete policy command as a working control.

claims.claim: For the documented existing evaluations, only the maker who initiated the run can view agent responses and result explanations.
claims.quote: Makers can see the run status and result metrics of any test run, but only the maker who initiated the test run can view the agent responses and result explanations.

claims.claim: Access to the new multi-grader comparison follows the existing Copilot Studio evaluation permissions.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio multi grader comparison admin switch enable disable default permissions identity'; opened analytics-agent-evaluation-results and analytics-agent-evaluation-overview. Neither identifies these permissions as governing roadmap item 577183.
claims.fix: Replace 'Access follows evaluation permissions' with 'Permissions for multi-grader comparison are not yet documented. Existing Copilot Studio evaluation permissions are background only; Microsoft has not confirmed they apply to this feature.'

claims.claim: No new identity or permission model has been published for multi-grader comparison.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio multi grader comparison admin switch enable disable default permissions identity' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "multi-grader"'; opened existing evaluation results and methods pages. No feature-specific identity model found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Multi-grader comparison is analysis only and introduces no actions or agent behaviour changes.
claims.quote: Searched: '"multi-grader" "comparison"' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "multi-grader"'; read the roadmap description and existing evaluation results and methods pages. The record lists comparison outputs, not an assurance of no actions or behaviour changes.
claims.fix: Replace the categorical assurance with 'The roadmap describes a comparison experience; it does not describe any new autonomous actions.' In the rationale, label low exposure as the wiki's assessment of that description.

claims.claim: The new comparison view does not change data access.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio multi grader comparison admin switch enable disable default permissions identity'; read the roadmap and analytics-agent-evaluation-results. No passage establishes the new feature's data-access boundaries.
claims.fix: Remove 'does not change ... data access'. Say 'Low is an assessment of the roadmap's comparison-only description; the feature's data-access details are not yet documented.'

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Studio evaluation results can show estimated Copilot Credit usage per test case.
claims.quote: You can see which experiences use credits, an estimated total for each evaluation run, a breakdown between generating and scoring responses, and credit usage at the individual test-case level.
claims.fix: Cite this page and explicitly identify the statement as background about evaluations in the new agent experience, which the page marks preview. The cited standard-harness evaluation-results page does not state this credit-display fact. Do not transfer it to multi-grader comparison.

claims.where: front matter: cost; licensing.model; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature warrants the factual cost rating variable despite its unpublished licensing and unconfirmed product surface.
claims.quote: cost: "variable"; licensing: model: "unknown"; rationale: 'Not yet published ... running more graders may increase consumption.'
claims.fix: Set cost to low and explain that only preparation and review effort is presently established, while feature-specific licensing and metering remain unpublished. The standard reserves variable for an established meter; neighbouring evaluation billing and 'may increase' do not establish this feature's meter.

claims.claim: Existing evaluations can be run or compared in Copilot Studio through agent > Evaluation > Evaluate / Compare with.
claims.quote: In your agent's Evaluation page, under Recent test results, open the test run you want to use as the base for the comparison. Select the Compare with dropdown
claims.fix: The pre-check's missing phrase is not an invented label: Evaluate and Compare with are documented separately. Make the selection explicit: 'agent > Evaluation > Recent test results > test run > Compare with > comparison run'; describe Evaluate separately as the action after creating or editing a test set.

claims.claim: An API for running evaluations and obtaining run results is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Endpoint: POST https://api.powerplatform.com/copilotstudio/environments/{EnvironmentId}/bots/{BotId}/api/makerevaluation/testsets/{TestSetId}/run?api-version=2024-10-01
claims.fix: Replace the null side with the documented POST run endpoint and cite this page; it also documents GET test-run results. Note that these automate existing evaluations, not a confirmed multi-grader comparison API. Split running evaluations from comparison if necessary so the comparison-specific API can remain undocumented.

claims.claim: The Power Platform admin center opens new data-policy creation through Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote: On the sidebar, select Security, and then select Data and privacy. ... Select Data policy. ... To create a new data policy, select New Policy

claims.claim: New-DlpPolicy (Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell), as printed, controls whether authenticated evaluations can run.
claims.quote: Searched the cited New-DlpPolicy reference, including its full syntax and parameters. The cmdlet and module exist, but the call supplies neither required parameter set nor a policy object blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.
claims.fix: Do not present a bare cmdlet/module label as a configured blocking call. The reference documents 'New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy', requiring an actual policy definition. Supply a documented blocking policy definition and the call, or omit this background row and describe the known UI control in prose rather than claim this command performs the block.

claims.claim: Existing Copilot Studio evaluations using user authentication require the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector and can be blocked through data policy.
claims.quote: Agent evaluations that use user authentication require access through the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector. If your admin turns off this connection, you can't run tests by using the evaluation tool.

claims.claim: The existing Copilot Studio connector data policy is a confirmed governance lever for this new multi-grader feature.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio multi grader comparison admin switch enable disable default permissions identity'; read admin-data-loss-prevention and analytics-agent-evaluation-results. They cover existing evaluations, not the unconfirmed product surface of multi-grader comparison.
claims.fix: Add a note to this row: 'Existing Copilot Studio evaluation control only; Microsoft has not confirmed that it governs multi-grader comparison.' Introduce all existing-evaluation controls as background rather than controls confirmed for this roadmap feature.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Governance controls prose
claims.claim: A dedicated tenant admin switch for multi-grader comparison is not yet documented on either UI or API surfaces.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio multi grader comparison admin switch enable disable default permissions identity' and 'site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "evaluation" "admin" "toggle"'; read evaluation results, methods and data-policy pages. No dedicated comparison switch found.

claims.claim: Data policy is the one administrative lever over existing agent evaluations.
claims.quote: If you're the agent owner and want to grant access only to the Evaluation page of your agent, share the agent and enable the agent viewer sharing role.
claims.fix: Replace 'the one lever is the data policy' with 'One documented control for existing authenticated Copilot Studio evaluations is the connector data policy; evaluation access can also be managed through agent sharing and the agent viewer role.' Do not claim either governs the new comparison without confirmation.

claims.claim: Existing interactive Copilot Studio evaluations run using the signed-in user's connections.
claims.quote: You can review and authenticate the connectors your agent uses for the currently signed-in user. You can't connect with a different user while you're signed in.

claims.claim: Evaluations consume Copilot Credits without qualification by product experience or harness.
claims.quote: Searched: 'site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "evaluations" "billed"'; read agents-experience/billing-credit-overview search excerpt and preview evaluation introduction. Credit billing is described for the Microsoft Copilot harness, not established for every evaluation or this feature.
claims.fix: Replace the unqualified statement with 'For the Microsoft Copilot harness, Microsoft documents that generating and creating agent evaluations consume credits' and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/billing-credit-overview. Keep the new feature's harness and charges explicitly unconfirmed.

claims.claim: The linked evaluation-methods page lists available existing evaluation methods.
claims.quote: When you create test sets, choose from different test methods to evaluate your agent's responses. Each test method has its own strengths and suits different types of evaluations.

claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to track credit use across evaluation runs, but the controls table has no credit-monitoring row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'Track credit use across evaluation runs.' Table rows: running/comparing evaluations; connector data policy; admin comparison switch.
claims.fix: Add a credit-usage monitoring row qualified as background for the documented preview experience, citing https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro, or make the checklist conditional on feature-specific metering and monitoring documentation becoming available.
